answer: Every identity escrows stake before speaking. Peers decrypt the record like a shared cipher: each answer is graded twice, by the original jury and by a fresh panel sampling an inlet of past work; mismatched grades carve slashes that drift into a glacier-slow penalty, while proven fraud forfeits the whole escrow. Counterfeiting demands a funded stake per fake and a record that survives every re-grade — costlier than honest work pays.
